about: The information architecture and brand of every documentation page. devrel/shell.mjs reads it to wrap the pages that crates/devrel (learn/) and builder/site.mjs (start/, examples/) write, and to write the docs hub, llms.txt and sitemap.xml. Pages carry their own Diátaxis type and journey stage; this file only names the allowed values, their order and their authorities.
name: Prism-DevRel

hub.title: Build apps that prove what they do
hub.lead: Prism is an open SDK for apps that prove what they do. Describe an app once, and Prism writes every part of it, checks every claim it makes, and ships it to run anywhere.
hub.body: This site shows you how to build Prism apps. Start with a tutorial. Follow a how-to guide for the task in front of you, and look up details in the reference. Read the explanations when you want to know why. Then copy an example, or study a whole project in a case study. The site is itself a Prism app: each page comes from a model, and is checked before it goes live.
hub.guides: The readers this site is written for, one for each stakeholder of the model. Each page names the guide it was written for.
hub.waysLead: Pick the one closest to what you have: an idea, existing code, or an app like yours.

app.about: The app page at the root, as a newcomer meets it: what the site is (app.json tagline), the ways on (app.json links, drawn by the frame under the description), and a verified app to try. devrel/shell.mjs checks the links are these and land on pages.

types.label: tutorial
types.what: Lessons that take you by the hand through building something, so you gain skill and confidence.

types.label: how-to guide
types.what: Directions that take you through the steps of a real task you already want to do.

types.label: reference
types.what: Technical descriptions of the machinery and how to operate it, to consult while you work.

types.label: explanation
types.what: Discussion that gives context and reasons, so you understand why Prism is the way it is.

journey.authority: Caroline Lewko and James Parton, Developer Relations: How to Build and Grow a Successful Developer Program, Apress, 2021, the developer journey

stages.label: Discover
stages.question: What is Prism, and is it for me?

stages.label: Evaluate
stages.question: Does Prism solve my problem, and can I trust what it claims?

stages.label: Learn
stages.question: How do I build my first working app?

stages.label: Build
stages.question: How do I make my app do what I need?

stages.label: Scale
stages.question: How do I ship, maintain and grow what I built?

collections.about: Beside the four Diátaxis types, two collections of worked material: example apps and case studies. A page joins a collection by <meta name="collection">, and is listed in that collection's tab instead of its Diátaxis type's tab, grouped by <meta name="collection-group">; it keeps its Diátaxis type and journey stage as labels. The collection's landing page is <path>index.html.
collections.authority: Caroline Lewko and James Parton, Developer Relations (Apress, 2021): sample applications serve the Build stage and customer case studies the Evaluate stage of the developer journey

items.label: example
items.what: Small apps, each built from one prompt and verified, grouped by the pattern they follow. Copy one and change it.

items.label: case study
items.what: Whole Prism projects, read record by record at a pinned commit, from their users to their proofs. Each one updates as its project grows.
